title: Dissociable behavioral and neurophysiological mediators of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and high intensity interval training (HIIT) success in cannabis use disorder
summary: In the research project “Dissociable mediators of success of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and high-intensity interval training (HIIT) for cannabis abstinence”, we are investigating the efficacy and underlying behavioral, psychophysiological and hormonal mechanisms of both interventions in people with cannabis use disorder. In this context, we are developing and testing the group manual CANnaQUIT - a behavioral and cannabis-specific cessation program based on CANDIS (Hoch et al., 2012), which has been expanded to include elements from other cannabis cessation guidelines (Rees et al., 1998; Steinberg et al., 2005). Participants are randomly assigned to one of three experimental conditions: One group receives exclusively the cannabis-specific cessation program CANnaQUIT, another group additionally undergoes exercise therapy with high-intensity interval training, while a further, third group is allocated to the waitlist-control group. This group receives no intervention during the study period. The aim of this intervention study is to evaluate the efficacy of the CANnaQUIT group therapy program and to compare the underlying differential mechanisms (behavioral, psychophysiological, hormonal) between these three groups in order to improve treatment options for people with cannabis use disorder in the long term and increase abstinence rates.

interventions.name: CBT group. This group only receives cannabis-specific cessation psychotherapy over a period of 12 weeks. The group sessions take place once a week over a period of 90 minutes.

CBT + HIIT group. This group receives cannabis-specific cessation psychotherapy over a period of 12 weeks. The group sessions take place once a week over a period of 90 minutes. 
In addition to CANnaQUIT, six supervised HIIT sessions are conducted within a two-week period (maximum 14 days), general
Waitlist control group. This group receives no intervention during the study period.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosed cannabis use disorder (DSM-V-TR)
Age 18-65 years
Exclusion criteria:
Acute (hypo-)manic episode remitted for less than 4 weeks  
Depressive episode remitted for less than 4 weeks 
Psychopharmacological treatment of bipolar disorder/ depressive episode less than 2 weeks stable 
Schizophrenia/ psychotic episode: fully remitted for less than 4 weeks  
Current psychotherapeutic or addiction-specific treatment (without possible break during the study) 
Daily intake of sedatives/ neuroleptics/ stimulants 
Current other moderate / severe substance use disorder apart from nicotine & cannabis
Current suicidal ideation or acute suicide risk
Medical contraindication to high-intensity interval training (HIIT)
